title: substitution-universality-class
description: An equivalence class of primitive non-singular step-n substitution rules under shift equivalence of their matrices: two rules lie in the same class iff their RG-flow classifying dynamics agree, i.e. their dimension groups are isomorphic as ordered abelian groups. Generated by quotienting step-n substitution rules by the shift-equivalence relation on their incidence matrices.

representative.description: a step-n substitution rule standing for its class; any rule whose matrix is shift equivalent to it inhabits the same class

shift-equivalence.description: the class relation: matrices M, M' are shift equivalent (SE) iff there are non-negative integer matrices R, S and an integer l >= 1 with M^l = RS and M'^l = SR; SE is the transitive closure of strong shift equivalence (M = RS, M' = SR)

dimension-group.description: DG(S) = the direct limit of Z^n under M^T with the order induced by the non-negative cone; the complete SE invariant, so the class is exactly an isomorphism class of dimension groups

perron-eigenvalue.description: the Perron-Frobenius spectral radius lambda_PF(M); the single most important numerical SE-invariant, equal across all members of the class

pisot-salem-type.description: the algebraic-number type of lambda_PF (Pisot or Salem); an SE-invariant coarser than the dimension group but finer than lambda_PF alone
